title: Narrative is the recurrent first-visible locus of pipeline hierarchy drift
description: Across the inspected runs, the Narrative stage most frequently shows the earliest observable departure from the requested company-first editorial hierarchy — turning a company introduction into a product/architecture-led story or adding unsupported audience/validation language.
audience: Content architects, experiment designers, product/content teams operating Nuëyon.Compose pipelines
rationale: Why it matters: If Narrative is the stage where the intended company-first story most often becomes product- or orchestration-first, then interventions that preserve story priority are likeliest to succeed when targeted at Narrative (prompt constraints, guardrails, checks). Prioritizing Narrative fixes limits rework downstream and focuses experimentation where the problem appears. Gaps and uncertainty: the evidence localizes the first observable shift but does not prove Narrative is the root cause in every run — some runs shift earlier (Idea or Synthesis) and Compose can amplify issues. A controlled trial is needed to confirm causation before large-scale process changes.
evidence: Explicit observations: Narrative is identified as the earliest visible hierarchy shift in Experiment 007 runs 001–002; Experiment 008 A-002; Experiment 009 baseline 002/003 and candidate runs 001–003. Cross-experiment summary states: “Narrative is the most recurrent first visible hierarchy shift in the available records.” The per-run tables show concrete Narrative-level examples (e.g., turning an orchestration product detail into the through-line, inventing audiences, adding validation framing). The report clarifies this is an observable stage-level pattern, not a demonstrated model causal chain.
